name: ECC
tagline: A free plugin that turns Claude Code into a full engineering team - 261 skills, 63 sub-agents, 79 commands.
sentence: Install ECC (Everything Claude Code) and your single Claude Code agent gains a roster of specialized sub-agents: one writes tests, one reviews security, one manages packages, one handles releases - 63 in total, coordinated by a guided installer.
replaces: Assembling your own collection of Claude Code plugins and CLAUDE.md rules

visual.alt: The ECC README header showing 'Everything Claude Code' with its tagline and install command, followed by sections for skills, sub-agents and commands, with badges showing 271K stars and MIT license.
visual.caption: ECC's README: 261 skills, 63 sub-agents and 79 commands, installed with one command.

board.say: Claude Code is powerful out of the box, but building a complete workflow - testing, security review, package management, releases - means assembling plugins one at a time.
board.eg: You need a test skill, a security reviewer, a docs generator and a release helper. Each one is a separate install, a separate config, a separate thing to maintain.

board.say: You run the ECC installer, pick a profile (minimal, core or full), and it sets up everything.
board.eg: `npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 setup` walks you through a guided install: pick minimal (essentials), core (recommended), or full (everything).

board.say: Your normal Claude Code prompts. ECC's skills and sub-agents activate based on what you're doing.
board.eg: Ask Claude Code to review a file and ECC's security sub-agent checks for vulnerabilities. Ask it to deploy and the deployment sub-agent handles the steps.

board.say: It adds 261 skills, 63 specialized sub-agents and 79 commands to your Claude Code, organized by category.
steps: Skills: specific behaviors like test-driven development, code review, documentation generation, security scanning
Sub-agents: specialized roles that handle focused tasks - one for tests, one for security, one for packages, one for releases
Commands: shortcuts for common workflows - run all checks, generate a changelog, create a release
board.eg: The creator won the Anthropic x Forum Ventures hackathon by building his entire platform (zenith.chat) through Claude Code configured with ECC's skills.

board.say: One agent that acts like a team - each task is handled by the right specialist.

outputs.eg: Claude Code with testing, security, deployment, documentation and 50+ other capabilities installed and configured
ECC works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini and Zed - same skills across different agents
The installer asks what you need and configures only those skills. No manual CLAUDE.md editing required.

before: Setting up a complete Claude Code workflow means finding, installing and configuring a dozen different plugins.
Each plugin has its own install process, its own rules, and its own way of conflicting with the others.
after: One installer, one setup, 261 skills and 63 sub-agents. Pick a profile and go.
Skills work across 6 different AI agents, so switching tools doesn't mean re-configuring everything.
uses_note: ECC has 271K stars and 268 contributors. Named third-party uses beyond the creator's own projects are sparse - adoption is broad but documented case studies from non-makers are thin.

uses.what: Won the Anthropic x Forum Ventures hackathon at Cerebral Valley, SF, building his zenith.chat platform entirely through Claude Code with ECC's config. First place among 100+ participants, $15K in Anthropic credits.
Used ECC with a local AI model (Omnicoder-9B via llama.cpp) to build a Python-based SQL Server MCP tool in one afternoon. Reported the system stayed on track and self-corrected without prompting.

steps: Run the guided installer: `npx ecc-universal@2.2.3 setup`. Pick the 'core' profile for a good starting set.
Open a project in [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview) and ask it to review a file for security issues - watch the security sub-agent handle it.
Try a few commands: ask it to run all checks, generate documentation, or set up a testing workflow.
try.paste:
/skillspector https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC

If that scan passes: run the guided installer with the 'core' profile, then test 3 different capabilities (security review, testing, and documentation). Report what each sub-agent does and whether the output is useful. 10 minutes max.

footprint.disk: No data found for exact size. 261 skills are primarily Markdown instruction files; sub-agents are config, not binaries.
footprint.memory: No measurable overhead beyond what Claude Code already uses. Skills are context instructions.
footprint.runs_on: Claude Code 2.1+, Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini, Zed. Needs Node.js 18+ and Git.

best_for: You want a complete Claude Code setup without assembling plugins one by one
You work across multiple AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) and want the same skills everywhere
skip_if: You prefer a minimal agent setup and don't want 261 skills in your context
You've already built a custom workflow that works - ECC may conflict with existing CLAUDE.md rules

alternatives.name: mattpocock/skills
alternatives.line: 27 focused, high-quality skills. Much smaller than ECC's 261, but each one is more carefully tested. A good choice if you want less, not more.

alternatives.name: Custom CLAUDE.md rules
alternatives.line: Write your own rules from scratch. The most control, the most work, and no sub-agents - but nothing you didn't put there yourself.

watch: **261 skills is a lot.** The full profile adds significant context to every agent interaction. The guided installer's 'minimal' profile exists for a reason.
**Named case studies from non-makers are thin.** 271K stars and 268 contributors, but published stories of 'I used ECC for my company and here's what happened' are hard to find.
**v2.0 is a recent rewrite.** ECC shipped v2.0.0 as a 'cross-harness agent system' - the architecture changed significantly, so earlier tutorials may not match the current setup.
**Potential conflicts with other plugins.** 261 skills and 63 sub-agents can conflict with other installed skills or CLAUDE.md rules. The guided installer helps, but check for overlaps.
